decision_conditions: Reason : 1 - The proposed additional storey, by reason of its height, scale, bulk, and mansard roof form, would result in a visually dominant and top-heavy addition that fails to appear subordinate to the host building. The proposal would disrupt the established proportions and roof form of the dwelling and appear incongruous within the context of the host property and the wider terrace. Furthermore, due to its prominent siting adjacent to a conservation area, the development would harm the setting of the adjacent conservation area. In these respects, the proposals would be contrary to Policies DC1, DC4 and DC8 of the Local Plan (2018).

Reason : 2 - The proposed development, by reason of its height, scale, and massing, including the introduction of a 75-degree sloping mansard roof, would result in an unacceptable overbearing impact and increased sense of enclosure to neighbouring properties, particularly Nos. 99, 97, 95, and 93 Chesson Road. The development would project above the existing flank wall and infringe the 45-degree guideline when assessed from the nearest habitable room windows, resulting in a harmful loss of outlook, particularly to windows at lower levels. As such, the proposal would fail to safeguard the amenities of neighbouring occupiers and is contrary to Policy H11 of the Local Plan (2018) and Key Principles HS6 and HS7 of the Planning Guidance SPD (2018).
description: Erection of an additional floor at roof level.
